messages:
Riley K.: Quick design review for the routing policies editor 1 1. Main asks: reduce visual noise in the rules list, make priority collisions more discoverable, and tighten empty-state copy.
Sam Wu: For noise, how about collapsing rules into match-type groups with a thin divider and subtle shadow when expanded? Keeps context but reduces length.
Aisha: Agree. Please surface a group-level validation dot so errors aren't hidden when collapsed. Could be a small red dot with count.
Noah: Drag & reorder note: if groups are collapsed, dropping between collapsed groups is ambiguous. Proposal: show a temporary drop placeholder line at the bottom of the target group while hovering. It should have clear text: "Drop here to add to {{group}}".
Riley K.: Love the placeholder idea. Make copy shorter: "Drop to add to {group}". And for collisions we should give inline suggestions: "This priority overlaps with rule X 1. Adjust to continue or create a tie-breaker."
Aisha: Accessibility: verify that the red error dot has an accessible name (e.g., aria-label="1 validation in header rules"). Also check color contrast: the error dot text fails at 3.2:1, needs to be >=4.5:1 for small text.
Sam Wu: UX copy tweak: change the rule action label from "fallback model" to "fallback model (secondary)" to clarify behavior. Tooltip: "Used when primary model rejects or fails." Small change but helps SREs.
Maya (design-bot): Automated note: accordions must use role="button" and include aria-expanded and aria-controls. Keyboard pattern: Enter/Space toggles, Arrow keys move between headers.
Noah: Preview simulator: add a "Simulate fallback" toggle and a small "confidence" column (low/med/high) so PMs can see likely degradation. Also show a yellow warning if fallback engages in >30% of requests.
Riley K.: Good. Add top-of-preview banner: "Simulation excludes caching and batching; latency is illustrative." Keep it subtle.
Aisha: Empty state copy: change CTA from "Create a rule" to "Add your first routing rule" 1 (more explicit). Also include a microcopy hint: "Start with a header or body match."
Sam Wu: Keyboard shortcut request: quick key ']' to toggle next group, '[' to previous. Might conflict though1 — open to better combos.
Maya (design-bot): Accessibility scan: banner contrast ok, but drop-placeholder text fails. Suggest color #0A66FF on white for buttons and #D32F2F for errors with white text to meet 4.5:1.
Noah: Implementation note: when a drop causes identical priorities, block the drop and surface a modal offering to auto-resolve by incrementing priority or to cancel. Modal copy: "Conflict detected: same priority assigned. Auto-resolve by nudging new rule to next available priority?" Buttons: "Auto-resolve" / "Cancel".
Riley K.: For the auto-resolve flow, add an inline fade animation to indicate the nudge and show a tiny toast: "Priority adjusted +1 to resolve conflict". Keep it non-fatal.
Aisha: Also ensure screen readers get notified. Use aria-live="assertive" for the modal announcement and polite for the toast.
Sam Wu: I'll wire the drag placeholder + modal in the sandbox. Tagging @Noah for the fallback sim wiring.
ci-bot: Sandbox build created: "routing-groups-accordion" - https://ci.redwood/sandbox/routing-groups-accordion (expires in 72h).
Riley K.: Thanks team. Action items: Sam - prototype placeholder + group pill; Aisha - run contrast and aria checks; Noah - preview sim and modal behavior; I'll update the figma frames and share link for dogfooding tomorrow.
Maya (design-bot): Figma proto: https://redwood.internal/figma/routing-groups-accordion 1. Automated color audit attached (fails: drop-helper, small error text).
Riley K.: Great. Let's try to dogfood by EOD tomorrow. If we hit a11y blockers hold the rollout.
Sam Wu: On it. Short follow-up question: should the group pill also show non-blocking warnings (yellow) for "potential collision"? I think yes, with tooltip: "Potential overlapping priority detected."
Aisha: Yes, show yellow for potential, red for blocking. Both clickable to expand and fix.
Noah: Cool. Will update PR once prototype validated.
Riley K.: Closing thread for now. Will post final copy variants (3 options) in the channel for quick A/B selection.
